req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. The pre-loaded fixture has exactly one post (id=1). Tests must cover: (1) positive — existing post id=1 returns 200 on GET update (proves the happy path and that 404 is not always returned); (2) negative — non-existent id returns exactly 404 on GET update, POST update, and POST delete; (3) boundary — id=0 (below minimum), id=2 (one above the only existing post), and a large id all return 404. Each test logs in as user 'test' (author of post 1) to satisfy login_required. Mutation resilience: exact status code assertions (catches 404->403, 404->400, 200->302 mutations), both sides of the existence check (id exists vs. id does not exist), boundary ±1 around the only valid id.

tests.name: test_update_existing_post_returns_200
preconditions: Database initialised with fixture data (post id=1, author user id=1)
expected: HTTP 200 response (post exists, user is author)
trace: R-FLASKR-022 — happy path: existing id must NOT return 404
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_existing_post_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200

test_update_existing_post_returns_200()

    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
